newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian lev closes at new low of 428-435 to dlr.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian lev closes at new low of 428-435 to dlr.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at a new low of 428-435 per dollar on Thursday from 425-430 morning levels on the interbank market amid persistently high dollar demand and limited support from the central bank, traders said.
"Large fuel importers continued bidding for large dollar volumes while supply was low and at increasingly high dollar levels," one dealer said.

The central bank (BNB) was seen covering part of the demand, partly relieving pressure on the lev and preventing a sharper fall, dealers said. BNB officials were not available for comment. The previous low for the lev was 415-418 on Wednesday.

High dollar demand from fuel importers amid insufficient supply has pressured the lev to its current levels from 362-364 on Monday as the central bank could not efficiently counter the slide because of a fall in its forex reserves, traders said.

The BNB said on Wednesday it would continue intervening on the local market to support the lev and would step up supervision to ensure that commercial banks adhere to its regulations concerning net open foreign currency positions.
The BNB also said its foreign exchange reserves fell by some $16 million to $525 million in November.

The BNB said last month it will aim to preserve reserves for a possible introduction of a tight monetary regime, called a currency board, under which the local currency in circulation must be matched by the amount of foreign exchange reserves. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032
